text: World War II, one of the most pivotal conflicts in modern history, lasted from 1939 to 1945. It began on September 1, 1939, when Nazi Germany, led by Adolf Hitler, invaded Poland, prompting the United Kingdom and France to declare war. Over the next six years, the war spread across the globe, involving more than 30 countries and claiming an estimated 50-80 million lives. The tide of the war turned in favor of the Allied Powers, led by the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Union, with key victories at Stalingrad (1943), D-Day (1944), and Hiroshima and Nagasaki (1945).
